written.stem: Describe the stages of aerobic respiration and state where each takes place in the cell.
written.model_answer: Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm, where glucose is split into two pyruvate with a net gain of 2 ATP. In the link reaction in the mitochondrial matrix, pyruvate is converted to acetyl CoA and carbon dioxide is released. The Krebs cycle in the matrix releases carbon dioxide and produces NADH and FADH2. Oxidative phosphorylation on the inner mitochondrial membrane uses an electron transport chain with oxygen as the final electron acceptor and produces most of the ATP.

points.text: Glycolysis in the cytoplasm: glucose to pyruvate
Link reaction in the matrix: acetyl CoA and CO2
Krebs cycle in the matrix: CO2, NADH, FADH2
Electron transport chain on the inner membrane
Oxygen is the final electron acceptor; most ATP made

samples.good: Glycolysis happens in the cytoplasm and splits glucose into two pyruvate, giving 2 ATP. In the link reaction in the mitochondrial matrix pyruvate becomes acetyl CoA and carbon dioxide is released. The Krebs cycle in the matrix releases carbon dioxide and makes NADH and FADH2. The electron transport chain on the inner membrane uses oxygen as the final electron acceptor and makes most of the ATP.
samples.partial: First glycolysis breaks glucose into pyruvate in the cytoplasm. Then the Krebs cycle happens in the mitochondria and makes carbon dioxide. At the end a lot of ATP is made.
samples.poor: Respiration is when we breathe in air and breathe out. It gives the body energy.

written.stem: Explain how urine is formed in a nephron of the human kidney.
written.model_answer: Blood enters the glomerulus at high pressure and small molecules such as water, glucose, urea and salts are forced into Bowman's capsule (ultrafiltration); blood cells and large proteins stay behind. In the proximal convoluted tubule all glucose and amino acids and much water and salt are selectively reabsorbed. The loop of Henle makes the medulla salty. In the distal tubule and collecting duct water is reabsorbed under the control of ADH, and the remaining fluid is urine.

points.text: Ultrafiltration in glomerulus into Bowman's capsule
Cells and large proteins not filtered
Selective reabsorption of glucose in the proximal tubule
Loop of Henle makes the medulla salty
Collecting duct reabsorbs water under ADH

samples.good: In ultrafiltration blood at high pressure in the glomerulus forces water, glucose, urea and salts into Bowman's capsule, but blood cells and large proteins stay in the blood. In the proximal tubule all the glucose and much water are reabsorbed by selective reabsorption. The loop of Henle makes the medulla salty. Water is reabsorbed from the collecting duct under the control of ADH, so concentrated urine is left.
samples.partial: Blood is filtered in the glomerulus into Bowman's capsule. Then glucose is reabsorbed back into the blood. The rest goes out as urine.
samples.poor: The kidney cleans the blood and makes urine which goes to the bladder.

written.stem: Explain a dihybrid cross between pure-breeding round yellow and wrinkled green pea plants, and how it supports Mendel's law of independent assortment.
written.model_answer: The parents RRYY and rryy produce gametes RY and ry, so the F1 are all RrYy with round yellow seeds. Each F1 plant produces four types of gamete, RY, Ry, rY and ry, in equal numbers because the alleles of the two genes assort independently. A 4 x 4 Punnett square gives an F2 phenotypic ratio of 9 round yellow : 3 round green : 3 wrinkled yellow : 1 wrinkled green. The appearance of new combinations (round green and wrinkled yellow) in this ratio supports the law of independent assortment.

points.text: Parental genotypes RRYY x rryy and F1 RrYy round yellow
Four gamete types in equal proportion

samples.good: Round yellow RRYY is crossed with wrinkled green rryy. All F1 are RrYy round yellow. The F1 make four types of gamete, RY, Ry, rY and ry, in equal numbers because the genes assort independently. A Punnett square of the F2 gives 9 round yellow, 3 round green, 3 wrinkled yellow and 1 wrinkled green, a 9:3:3:1 ratio. The new combinations round green and wrinkled yellow show independent assortment.
samples.partial: The F1 plants are all round and yellow. When they are crossed the F2 has a ratio of 9:3:3:1.
samples.poor: Mendel used peas. Some were round and some were wrinkled.

uploads.title: Photosynthesis overview
uploads.summary: These notes explain photosynthesis in two stages. The light-dependent reactions on the thylakoid membranes split water, release oxygen and make ATP and NADPH. The Calvin cycle in the stroma uses that ATP and NADPH to fix carbon dioxide with the enzyme Rubisco and make sugars. Light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature are limiting factors.
key_points: Light-dependent reactions: thylakoids, photolysis of water, O2 released
ATP and NADPH carry energy to the Calvin cycle
Rubisco fixes CO2 to RuBP in the stroma

uploads.title: Nerve impulses and synapses
uploads.summary: These notes describe the structure of a neuron, how a resting potential is kept by the sodium-potassium pump, how an action potential is produced by sodium and potassium ion movement, and how impulses cross a synapse using neurotransmitters.
key_points: Depolarisation by Na+ entry; repolarisation by K+ exit

uploads.title: Protein synthesis
uploads.summary: These notes explain how the base sequence of a gene is used to make a protein. In transcription RNA polymerase makes mRNA from the template strand in the nucleus. In translation ribosomes read the mRNA codons and tRNA molecules bring the matching amino acids, which are joined by peptide bonds.
key_points: Transcription in the nucleus by RNA polymerase
Codons are triplets; AUG starts translation
tRNA anticodons pair with codons on the ribosome
